ns2:section.sectionText: Adventures in Dictionaries - Dictionaries are strange objects: so revered as to receive special seating on purpose-build pedestals in libraries; so trusted that we dismiss even our own words as "not words" when they're not dictionaries; so impersonal and encompassing in their accounts of language that they feel almost authorless; and so irrelevant in online environments where definitions reach us through pop-ups and search summaries from nowhere. This seminar explores the genre of the dictionary--what it is, where it came from, why it matters. In addition to researching the history of major mainstream dictionaries, we'll explore strange and subversive dictionaries--visual dictionaries, slang dictionaries, sex dictionaries, and more. We'll investigate how dictionaries are made and revised, and ask which practices align with present political urgencies to do with identity and identification. Finally we'll consider how dictionaries are received and reinvented by readers, users, poets, artists, legal experts, cultural critics, and more.
